fingerprint.signature: A Git fetch outlives the systemd start deadline, SIGTERM leaves an empty agent.lock directory, and every later timer poll fails with dispatch_agent_already_running although no owner process exists.
stableConditions: The fixed dispatch service is killed while the old directory-only lock is held.
The old agent removes the lock only through its normal finally path and stores no verifiable owner identity.
observedEvidence: The production journal records a poll start at 2026-07-26 14:09:36 +08:00 and a 180-second systemd timeout with SIGTERM at 14:12:36.
The target retained an empty mode-700 ubuntu-owned agent.lock with no fuser, pgrep or lslocks owner.
The journal recorded 4,526 dispatch_agent_already_running failures before the repair acceptance.

rootCause.conclusion: The old agent combined an unbounded Git child with a directory-only lock that had no owner record or stale-owner recovery, so an external process termination permanently disabled the polling channel.
evidence: The lock mtime equals the start of the timed-out poll and predates all repeated already-running failures.
No live process owned the lock, while deleting or bypassing the lock was not required to reproduce the old failure.
The new agent recovered the same stale empty lock on Linux and immediately consumed the expired dispatch as non-reusable.
Git children now have a hard 90-second timeout that callers cannot disable, below the 180-second systemd deadline.
The SSH wrapper bounds connection attempts and keepalive failure detection.

The lock records boot ID, PID, Linux process-start identity and a random token; live owners remain fail-closed, proven-dead owners are quarantined, and an unowned legacy lock is recoverable only after four minutes.

regression.redCase: Killing the old poll after lock acquisition leaves an empty directory that permanently blocks every later dispatch.
